method: Each chain in ATTACK_CHAIN_TEMPLATES was given a minimal POSITIVE fixture containing exactly the failing findings needed to satisfy its requires/min_matches (and nothing that should trigger a different chain), and a NEGATIVE fixture that is the same configuration with ONLY the chain's break_rule_id finding remediated. Expected verdicts below were derived by reading the rule evaluate() semantics and correlate_attack_paths' union-of-failed-rule-ids logic BEFORE any test ran against these fixtures. The engine's actual verdict must match exactly; any deviation is reported as a loud failure, not silently adjusted.

_fixture_design_notes.CHAIN-NET-MGMT-TAKEOVER: Positive uses a config with NO VTY lines, 'aaa new-model' PRESENT, and NO remote logging host. The three failed requires are exactly {CIS-CISCO-1.1.6 (no vty), CIS-CISCO-1.1.8 (no vty), CIS-CISCO-1.3.1 (no logging)}: of the 4 requires only these 3 fail (1.1.1 passes via aaa), hitting full chain requires union with exactly one chain. Missing aaa instead would re-fire CHAIN-NET-WEB-EXPLOITATION via {1.1.8, 1.1.1}; adding a VTY block (to fail 1.1.6 without truncating) would re-fire CHAIN-NET-WEB-EXPLOITATION (if 1.1.1 also fails) or CHAIN-NET-SPOOFING-BYPASS (1.1.8 without access-class). The NIST correlates that feed WB-MGMT-TAKEOVER stay sub-threshold here (only AU-2 fails from no logging; AC-17/AC-3 pass with no vty lines, IA-2 passes with aaa). The negative therefore re-adds a single VTY block with ssh + access-class + exec-timeout to fix 1.1.8 (which necessarily also resolves 1.1.6/1.1.4), leaving only 1.3.1 failing.
_fixture_design_notes.whitebox_fixtures: AU-2 (remote syslog) always fails on whitebox/unknown-vendor configs because the structural mapping path does not populate logging fields; this is an inherent engine property, not extra fixture content.
